text:
The bar chart is built: 6 s, 1920×1080, light background (#F8FAFC).

- **Title** (top-left, 64 px bold) with a "USD, millions" subtitle. It fades and rises in from 0 s.
- **Axis** (**Axis line**) draws in from the left, 0.2–0.8 s. It is first in the sequence, as you asked.
- **Bars** (**Bar Q1**, **Bar Q2**, **Bar Q3**) grow up from the baseline at 0.9, 1.1 and 1.3 s, Quart Out, 0.6 s each. Heights are 20 px per $M, so 12, 18 and 15 are 240, 360 and 300 px.
- **Bar Q4 (highlight)** is blue (#2563EB) and grows at 1.5 s. It then overshoots to 106% and settles at 2.1–2.7 s, which is the extra pop.
- **Value labels** (12, 18, 15) fade and rise 14 px above each bar as it lands. The 27 is larger, blue, and springs in with a back ease at 2.1 s.
- **Quarter labels** Q1–Q4 sit under the baseline. Q4 is blue and bold to match the highlight.

Two things to know:
- The value labels fade and rise rather than count up. A true number count needs a text animator I didn't use here. Say if you want the count.
- Motion ends at 2.7 s, so the last 3.3 s is a static hold. I left it static because a slow push on the Q4 bar would distort the highlight. The critic flagged this; I can add a slow push to the whole chart if you'd prefer the hold to move.

I also moved the title and subtitle in from the edge to clear the title-safe margin.
